title: Two first knots under one count and under the fewest counts
claim: S1: a start of knots with no common neighbour grows as independent pieces, one per start knot, each a single seed on its open distinctions. S2: under one count, two first knots of a and b places grow together exactly when c = a = b (apart) or c = a - 1 = b - 1 (sharing one distinction), as two copies of N^c; otherwise a stall by round 4; a four-place knot presented as two three-place knots through a hidden distinction grows only at c = 2. S3: under the fewest counts, separate knots close; two knots sharing one distinction grow two copies of N^2 forever for every pair of sizes. S4: cheapness prefers the least admissible count.
standard_statement: Upward closure (cube condition) of a cover graph from several constraints; vertex splitting of parity constraints.
prior_work: FRESH-COUNT-20261118-001A (one seed); PICK-TWO-20261118-001 (betweenness analogue); GROWTH-LAW-20261107-001 (a beginning is a knot, another sense).
